newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish LPG consumption seen nearly doubling by 200.
newsitem.headline: Polish LPG consumption seen nearly doubling by 200.

text.p: Poland is likely to nearly double its liquified petroleum gas (LPG) consumption to 1.2 million tonnes annually in the year 2000, the chairman of the gas producers and distributors organisation said on Thursday.

"In 2000, liquid gas consumption should reach about 1.2 million tonnes, of which 80 percent will be imported," Adam Kubiak, head of the Polish Liquid Gas Organisation, said during a conference in Warsaw.
Current LPG consumption is 690,000 tonnes annually.
Kubiak said Poland's average per capita LPG consumption was about 18 kg annually, compared with 30 kg in Western countries.
The number of Polish cars using propane and butane was forecast to increase to 250,000 in the year 2000 from the current 150,000.
